name: Benedictine Convent of St John at Müstair
description: Tucked into a quiet Alpine valley in Graubünden, close to the Italian border, this Benedictine convent has been home to a religious community since around 800. Its church walls still carry Switzerland's largest collection of figurative murals from that Carolingian era, layered with later Romanesque frescoes and stucco work. It is a rare chance to see art more than 1,200 years old.
